close_reason: Removing the call_id clone from JmapRequestBuilder::add_call requires either Rc<String> (adds runtime cost), restructuring to push-then-check-then-pop (uglier), or hashing into HashSet<u64> (loses exact-string error message). For typical short call_ids (~5-10 bytes), the clone is cheap. Trade-off doesn't justify the API/code churn. Won't fix in 0.1.x; revisit if a future profile flags this as a hot spot.
description: src/request.rs:67-73 — `if !self.call_ids.insert(call_id.clone()) { return Err(...with call_id) } self.method_calls.push((..., call_id))`. Clones the call_id String into the HashSet, then pushes the original into method_calls. Idiomatic alternative: use HashSet::contains first to check, then insert/push without clone (one extra hash but no allocation). Or use Entry API. Or: insert into HashSet first (taking ownership), and if it returns false (was already present), reconstruct the call_id for the error message from the original args. The current implementation prefers correctness over micro-efficiency, but the pattern is the textbook 'clone to escape borrow' that idiomatic Rust readers flag. Note: locked crate.
title: JmapRequestBuilder::add_call clones call_id to insert into HashSet
